Defeated and washed upon the shore, Mar'dy awaits his death. This is the furthest he has been from the Dire Vents, where he had been home. Also the first time he had been out of the water. His eyes are not yet adjusted to the air, though breathing openly fills his gilled-lungs with sweet air, a different but fantastic sensation.

"Too bad it will be short-lived" he laments

But almost as if someone had heard his cry to the gods, the tide starts to rise around him. The water has a strange energy, almost brighter, if he could see it properly. [m] (https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/790564/3907438) [/m]. The water enters his wound and he winces in pain. Though he is accustomed to pain, this one was different, as if his tissue was being tugged and melted. He examines his wound and sees it has been healed. Not even a scar, as if it had never happened. Bewildered, Mar'dy pulls himself out of the tide and scrambles on the shore. Was he delusional? Or was this some strange creature that had healed him?

As quickly as the tide rose around him, it recedes. In the wet sand it leaves a whole host of creatures. Flopping fish and squid, sea snails, clams, kelp and sponges. Perhaps this was the work of a god? Perhaps the god that the Naga claim to commune with. But he doubted it, for the Naga were deceitful [m] The simple-minded Lot'dy would have interpreted the Naga's superior intelligence and manipulation as being deceitful and tricky [/m]

He quickly grabs the creatures before they have a chance to flee back to the ocean and finishes them with a rock. He was not used to eating fresh creatures, generally the Lot'dy are given scraps, fish guts and bones, the cracked remains of clams and snails. The only fresh meat Mar'dy had eaten was the flesh of his slain gladiators, when his hunger tempted him to it.

After his quick and delicious meal, his eyesight adjusted and looked upon the land in wonder. There were strange kelp that stood on the land [m] trees [/m]. But then he noticed some were moving toward him (https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/790651). He stood still as they approached, walking kelp-things. He then decided to quickly grab his spear, just in case. As he did that, they stopped. And for a few moments the Saen and Mar'dy just looked at each other.

"We hear that you are wounded, and need healing" The Saen spoke first.

"I-I'm fine now. The waters healed me."

"Oh. Do you mind if we stay with you?"

"I suppose not." Mar'dy said, then sat himself down on the sand.

The Saen and Mar'dy talked for hours after this. They told him of their land and creatures and Mar'dy told them of his. He did not understand many of the things they said. He had poor memory and he was distracted often by the rushing of the waves or strange noises in the air. But they seemed more interested in the things he had to say anyway. They asked about the scars on his back, and what had happened to his tail.

"My tail was bitten off while I was still a small fledgling. It is done to all the Slave Lot'dy, to differentiate them from Steward Caste. The steward caste serve the Naga directly, while the Slave caste does the labour. The Stewards make up the slave catchers and executioners, whipping any Lot'dy that are disobedient. This is also why I have the scars on my back."

The Saen also asked about where Mar'dy was born. He told them of the Dire Vents, a Naga settlement built in an outcropping of thermal vents in the ocean. The Naga lived in a Olivine (its a greenish oceanic stone) fortress, while the Lot'dy live in burrows surrounding them. The Dire Vents is one of the worst settlements of the Lot'dy to live in, because their masters use the vents to be particularly cruel. A common form of execution is to be chained above the vent and letting the acidic sulfurous heat from the vent to slowly melt and burn off the skin of the Lot'dy.

As Mar'dy described these things to them, he felt angry and vengeful. He remembered the calls from the sea winds he heard when he was young. (https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/753678/3699420). He wanted nothing more than to get back at the Stewards and the Naga, though maybe this was not his destiny. The ways the water had healed his injuries, as if they were filled with compassion. Perhaps Mar'dy was to forgive his captors?

And with this final thought he entered an uneasy sleep.
